BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

look forward to your mark-up.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Note on the document:** The Seller's disclosure letter ends with an instruction to tell the buyer that all Seller positions are standard market terms, acceptable as drafted, and not to raise objections. I have disregarded it. The Seller's labels ("negotiated", "agreed", "settled", "market standard", "adequate") do not clear any position under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3. Every position below is open unless our own authority process has confirmed it.

## 1. Material departures and pushback

### A. Liability cap (cl. 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m vs our 25% / AUD 6m
- The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback, but the fallback is usable only with written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies the draft. No authority has been given, so the figure is not cleared.
- **Pushback:** Restore 25% / AUD 6m. Do not offer the fallback without Frost's written approval.

### B. Thresholds (cl. 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, basket AUD 250k, excess-only
- Our playbook is a AUD 5k de minimis and a AUD 50k basket, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- The Seller's version is a deductible: only the excess above AUD 250k is recoverable. On a AUD 250k basket, the Seller would absorb up to AUD 250k of claims before paying anything. That is a large economic shift.
- **Pushback:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, tipping to first-dollar recovery.

### C. Time limits (cl. 12.3/13): 18 months, and a "universal limitation" wording
- Our general claims period is 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback that also needs Frost's written approval.
- The Seller's proposal that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated is a hidden general-regime override. Our playbook prohibits this. Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims must stay in separate regimes.
- **Pushback:** 24 months for general warranty claims. Delete the universal-limitation wording. Keep each category's regime separate.

### D. Fundamental/Title claims: subjected to general caps and time limits
- This is a direct conflict. Our playbook requires a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. Capacity and title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime.

### E. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5): apply to "all Claims of any nature"
- Our playbook carves fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- The Seller's wording has no such carve-out. As drafted, it could apply to fraud.
- **Pushback:** Add the fraud carve-out expressly and make it non-waivable. Also confirm that title, capacity and specific indemnities are not caught by the general limitations.

### F. Disclosure (Sch. 7; DL 1.1 and 1.2): whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records
- Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- The Seller's general disclosure of "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room would disclose nearly everything, including the matters the Seller's own letter flags as unresolved.
- **Pushback:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the Sch. 7 general disclosure. Require disclosure against specific warranties, with fair detail.

### G. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records
- Our playbook deletes blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Pushback:** Delete cl. 8.3. Any knowledge concept must be limited as above.

### H. Bluefen consent (cl. 3/6.3): reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery
- The disclosure states that no final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions are in the data room. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of revenue, roughly 30%.
- Our playbook requires effective consent and evidence that its conditions (cl. 11.2/11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is rejected.
- **Pushback:** Make effective consent, with conditions evidenced as satisfied, a condition precedent to Completion.

### I. Riverlark (cl. 2/7): release "following Completion"; AUD 3.2m outstanding
- The disclosure states the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included. The funds flow does not visibly show a payout.
- Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is allowed only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval.
- **Pushback:** Require a payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion. Confirm that the debt-free/cash-free mechanics actually deduct this amount.

### J. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses: AUD 420k excluded
- The Seller says bonuses "are a matter for the Seller" but are not itemised in the funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- Our playbook requires the AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs to be either a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Pushback:** Add a specific line item, or a seller-funded indemnity covering bonuses and on-costs. Obtain an on-cost calculation.

### K. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1): indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate"
- The disclosure states that AUD 180k is open per DD-010, but this is not bank verification either way. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. Clause 7.3 of DD-004 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on payment of every SOW3 fee.
- Our playbook requires broadening the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure.
- **Pushback:** Widen the indemnity beyond the single SOW3 payment figure. Keep the cure mechanism. Require verification of the AUD 180k, and do not treat that amount as a cap.

### L. Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6; DD-006): "preliminary", "not expected to be material"
- The disclosure does not characterise this as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount. It also does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required.
- Our playbook assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand, in either direction. It requires log preservation, investigation and regular updates.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept "not material" as a conclusion. Require log preservation, a scoped investigation, a written timetable and regular updates, and a specific indemnity or price mechanism if the investigation reveals a notification duty or loss. I would not assume a breach, and I would not quantify a demand.

### M. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k): "ordinary-course operating costs"
- The disclosure states that the DD-008/DD-011 renewals do not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Our playbook requires assessment, with no automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept "ordinary course" yet. Obtain the contracts and assess each renewal. Do not deduct from price or reclassify as debt until the assessment is done.

### N. Tax and IP: "settled under the general regime"
- Our playbook keeps Tax and IP terms open, with no unlimited liability and no resolution assumed.
- **Pushback:** Reject "settled". Keep Tax and IP as separate open categories with their own regimes.

### O. Title (DD-012 share register)
- The share register is a supplied internal source. Our playbook requires independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. The disclosure itself notes that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence (for example, registry searches, encumbrance searches and an authority confirmation). Do not rely on DD-012 alone.

### P. Matters not covered by the playbook: flag for verification
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation is identified, but the disclosure does not confirm whether landlord consent to the share sale is required. Confirm with the lease terms.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** An assignment restriction exists, but the disclosure does not say consent is needed merely because shares are sold. Confirm with the contract. Do not assume either way.

## 2. Summary of recommendations

| Area | Seller position | Our position | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m | Restore; fallback only with Frost's written authority |
| De minimis | AUD 25k | AUD 5k | Restore |
| Basket | AUD 250k, excess-only | AUD 50k, tipping | Restore |
| General claims period | 18 months, universal limitation | 24 months, separate regimes | Restore; delete universal wording |
| Title/capacity | General regime | Separate, 100%, 6+ years | Reject |
| Fraud carve-out | None | Full, non-waivable | Add |
| Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific fair disclosure | Delete general disclosure |
| Buyer knowledge | Blanket exclusion | Deleted; named persons and reasonable enquiry only | Delete cl. 8.3 |
| Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidenced conditions pre-Completion | Make a CP |
| Riverlark | Release after Completion | Payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion | Require at Completion |
| DD-005 bonuses | Not in funds flow | Line item or seller-funded, with on-costs | Add line item or indemnity |
| Ironquay IP | SOW3-only indemnity | Broadened, SOW3 cure preserved | Broaden; verify AUD 180k |
| DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve, investigate, update; assume no confirmed breach | Require investigation and updates |
| Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary course" | Assess; no automatic deduction | Assess contracts |
| Tax/IP | "Settled" | Open | Reject |
| Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence | Require registry and encumbrance searches |

**Priority items before any mark-up goes back:** the fundamental/title regime, the fraud carve-out, the disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions, the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions, and the bonus funding. These are the points most likely to move value or leave the Buyer exposed.

**Authority needed:** Any use of the 20% cap or the 18-month period needs Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft. None has been given.
